hens_rule_text: Hens may be kept for non-commercial purposes with no numeric cap in the code, as long as they stay in a securely enclosed yard or pen and at least 20 feet from neighboring dwellings.
permit_notes: The hen exception in Sec. 4-5(d)(2) needs no permit. Special permits from the city commission apply only to livestock or fowl kept for exhibition and display.
setback_notes: Hens must be kept no closer than 20 feet to neighboring dwellings.
coop_rules: Hens must be confined in a securely enclosed yard or pen at all times.
zoning_notes: Only non-commercial keeping is allowed. One rooster may be kept alongside hens for flock sustainability. Fowl on tracts of 5 or more contiguous acres are exempt from the section, and animals lawfully kept when the 2010 ordinance passed are grandfathered.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Read Sec. 4-5 in the city's own PDF of Chapter 4 (Ord. No. 10-O-15AA, 2010). No amendment since 2010 was found in searches, though the PDF date is not stated. Noise and sanitation nuisance rules still apply to roosters.
